gap: No result ChatGPT got states any measured idle draw for a 12V split-phase candidate. The closest named measurement is Victron community user rslifkin's reading of 9–10 W no-load on a MultiPlus Compact 12/2000/80-50 120V, against a 9 W spec. That is a sibling of the MultiPlus-II, not a candidate.
standout_why: I compared against victronenergy.com/inverters-chargers/help-me-choose (cited) and victronenergy.com/inverters-chargers/multiplus-ii-2x-120v (cited). Neither has an idle or efficiency figure: the product page lists only VA/W, peak, charge current, transfer switch, size and weight, and help-me-choose sends readers to datasheets. The other top results are Victron datasheets and brochures, an EG4 page and retailer listings, which carry maker specs at best. So no rival has a third-party measurement. But I could not find a named reviewer or lab that measured the candidates themselves (SunGoldPower LFP4K12V240VSP, AIMS PICOGLF40W12V240VS, MultiPlus-II 12V 2x120V). The only named reading I could open is on a different Victron model, so it adds little.
decides: It does not decide the pick. No named measurement exists for the 4,000 W 12V low-frequency split-phase units ChatGPT ranked first and second, so nothing measured backs or contradicts their idle and efficiency claims. The one opened owner reading (Victron Compact 12/2000, 9–10 W against a 9 W spec) only hints that Victron's 12V idle specs are realistic. The pick-relevant fact is still Victron's own statement that the MultiPlus-II 2x120V puts out 120V single phase in inverter mode, so it cannot make 240V from a 12V battery alone. ChatGPT's answer already says this. The page should frame the AIMS and SunGoldPower units as the only true 12V-to-240V options in the results, and present their idle figures as maker specs, not test results.
